title: Set the MTU size for a network interface
summary: Change the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) size for a network interface. This is used to optimize network performance, often for jumbo frames.

steps.explain: Use `sudo ip link set` with the `mtu` option to set the new MTU size.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface.

placeholders.name: MTU_SIZE
placeholders.description: The new MTU size in bytes (e.g., 9000 for jumbo frames).

alternatives.explain: Use the short form `sudo ip l s`.

placeholders.name: INTERFACE
placeholders.description: The name of the network interface.

placeholders.name: MTU_SIZE
placeholders.description: The new MTU size in bytes.

rollback.explain: To revert to the default MTU (usually 1500), set it back to 1500.

warnings: Incorrect MTU settings can cause packet fragmentation or dropped packets.
